title: Is Duolingo Stock a Buy?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc keeps Duolingo on HOLD with medium conviction, saying it is 'moving much closer' to a buy but not there yet. Management's response to the AI threat — focusing on the free product and putting monetisation second — is working: daily active user growth accelerated to 23% and then 29% in the last two quarters, and management plans to focus more on monetisation in 2027, including a chess product that already has 10 million daily active users. But expenses are expected to grow faster than revenue as product investment continues. EPS prospects collapsed from over 50% growth to minus 30% in mid-2025 on the AI scare, and have only recovered to about 8% a year. The freemium focus is biting into margins: cash flow from operations to sales fell from a 40% peak to about 37%, and the operating margin from 15% to 12.5%. The balance sheet is strong, with over $1.3bn in cash and short-term investments against just $84m of debt. At a forward P/E of 21.8 the stock looks relatively cheap versus its own history, and his revised DCF puts it fairly valued (exact fair value garbled in captions) versus a $170 price that has almost doubled from its $88 52-week low. He stresses the stock is riskier today than before ChatGPT. Calls: DUOL HOLD at $170, reiterated.
